title: Sunday Sketch
premise: A short branching romance vignette in which Mia spends a quiet Sunday in the park and decides how warmly to respond when Leo asks to share her bench and talk about sketching.
interaction_model: Tap-to-advance narrative scene with typewriter dialogue, two binary choice moments, ending branches, restart flow, and optional mute control.
objective: Guide the encounter toward the emotional outcome you want, ranging from a shared sketchbook connection to a reserved or solitary ending.
progression: Start screen -> introductory narration -> Leo arrives -> first choice about sharing the bench -> follow-up conversation if accepted -> second choice about engaging further -> one of three endings -> replay.
theme: Romantic slice-of-life park encounter framed as a sketchbook scene.
mood: Dreamy, tender, reflective, and lightly bittersweet depending on the branch taken.
likely_audience: players who enjoy short interactive stories
casual mobile players who prefer low-pressure narrative choices
confidence_notes: High confidence that this is a compact story-choice experience built around dialogue and branching endings.
High confidence that the intended emotional axis is openness versus reserve.
Moderate confidence on category naming because the provided universe does not include a direct visual novel label.
recreation_prompt: Create a short, polished mobile-friendly interactive romance scene called "Sunday Sketch" presented like a dreamy visual-novel vignette. The player follows Mia during a quiet Sunday afternoon in a park while a stranger named Leo approaches and asks to share her bench. Use a full-screen illustrated background, softly staged character sprites, a glassy dialogue box, speaker name tag, circular portrait, typewriter text reveal, gentle music, light UI click and outcome sounds, and a start screen, mute button, and replayable ending screen. The gameplay loop should be simple: tap to advance dialogue, occasionally choose between two dialogue responses, and branch into three emotional outcomes. The first choice should decide whether Mia lets Leo sit beside her, and if she does, a second choice should decide whether she opens up and compares sketch notes or keeps the interaction polite and distant. The best ending should feel like a shared artistic connection, the middle ending should feel calm and restrained, and the lowest ending should return the park to solitude. Include subtle reaction feedback when choices are made, smooth character transitions on the canvas, and a soft romantic tone with moonlit or sun-dappled story-panel presentation cues.
